skill.name: run-linters
skill.description: Runs repository linters after code changes, reviews lint results, and guides fixes until checks pass.
skill.summary: Run configured repository linters after code changes and resolve reported issues.
skill.author: Cloud-Officer

content.value_statement: Code changes often introduce lint errors that slow reviews and releases. This skill runs configured linters and guides fixes until the checks pass.
actual_capabilities: Runs the repository linters command after a logical set of code changes.
Reviews lint output and identifies files that need fixes.
Edits affected files to resolve reported lint issues.
Re-runs linters to confirm fixes before completion.
Asks before disabling a lint rule that appears incorrect.
limitations: Depends on the repository lint configuration being present and correct.
Does not run after every small edit by design.
Does not replace tests, builds, or security scanners.
May need user input before changing lint rules or project standards.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Run linters after a feature branch is ready and fix issues before review.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Refactors
use_cases.description: Check formatting and style after broad edits that touched multiple files.

use_cases.title: Verify Agent Changes
use_cases.description: Confirm AI-assisted edits still meet repository lint standards before handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Lint Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner verification after small work is complete.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the lint checks for this repository and tell me whether anything needs to be fixed.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Lint Failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Standard cleanup after lint output reports issues.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the linters, fix any reported issues, and re-run the checks until they pass.

prompt_templates.title: Pre-Review Validation
prompt_templates.scenario: Pull request preparation before requesting review.
prompt_templates.prompt: After my recent changes, run the configured linters and resolve blocking lint errors before I open a pull request.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Repeated Failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced troubleshooting when lint failures persist.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the linters, group failures by cause, fix clear issues, and ask before changing any lint rule or project convention.

output_examples.input: Run lint checks after updating the authentication files.
output_examples.output: The lint run found style issues in two changed files. I fixed them and confirmed the next lint run passed.

output_examples.input: Check whether my refactor is ready for review.
output_examples.output: The repository linters completed successfully. No lint changes are needed before review.

output_examples.input: Fix the lint failures from my latest changes.
output_examples.output: I fixed the reported unused import and formatting issues. One rule change looked project-specific, so I asked before modifying it.

best_practices: Run this skill after a complete set of related code changes.
Review any proposed lint rule changes before accepting them.
Pair lint checks with tests or builds when release confidence matters.
anti_patterns: Do not run linters after every tiny edit in an active coding loop.
Do not disable lint rules just to make the check pass.
Do not treat a clean lint result as proof that behavior is correct.

faq.question: What command does this skill run?
faq.answer: It runs the repository linters command defined for this workflow.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it after a logical set of code changes or before a pull request.

faq.question: Will it fix lint issues automatically?
faq.answer: It can edit affected files for clear lint issues and then re-run checks.

faq.question: Does it run tests too?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on lint checks, not full tests or builds.

faq.question: Can it change lint rules?
faq.answer: It should ask before disabling or changing a lint rule.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
